description:
Demolition of two of three existing garages; replacement by single storey side extension, basement beneath extension with attached wall in front of new amenity space.
Replacement of Front Elevation Timber Sash single glazed windows to Timber sash double glazed windows
decision_conditions:
The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

<div>Prior to superstructure works, a detailed specification, a drainage layout, and a management &amp; maintenance plan (where applicable) of the bioretention planter box and living roof (substrate depth of 80-150mm excluding the vegetative mat) shall be submitted to and approved by the LPA, in consultation with the LLFA. It must be demonstrated that there will be no increase in surface water flow being discharged offsite and an overall reduction in peak flow rate and volume. The development shall be implemented as per the approved details.&nbsp;<br></div><p style="line-height: 1.38; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><br></p><p style="line-height: 1.38; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">REASON: In the interests of sustainable drainage.</p>

<p>All new external facing and roofing materials in respect of all the works hereby approved (and any other incidental works carried out in this connection) shall match those of the existing building in respect of materials used, detailed execution and finished appearance, including type, size, colour, bond, pointing, coursing, jointing, profile and texture.</p><p><br></p><p>

REASON: To preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the&nbsp;Graham Road and Mapledene Conservation Area.</p>

<p>No works shall commence on site (including demolition and site clearance) unless a Tree Protection Plan (“TPP”) to BS5837:2012 (or any standard that reproduces or replaces this standard) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The TPP shall detail the methods of tree/hedge protection and clearly detail the position and specifications for the erection of tree protective fencing and installation of ground protection, and a programme for its implementation. This shall include protection for the stem and planting pit of T1 as identified in the submitted Arboricultural Impact Assessment by Canopy Consultancy, dated February 2026. The works shall not be carried out unless in accordance with the approved details, and the measures specified by the TPP shall remain in place until the completion of the construction.<br style=""><br style="">REASON: &nbsp;To safeguard existing trees in the interests of visual amenity. Approval is required upfront to ensure that important trees are not permanently damaged or lost.</p>

<p>The works hereby approved shall not be carried out unless in accordance with the approved Arboricultural Method Statement by Canopy Consultancy, dated February 2026.&nbsp;<br style=""><br style="">REASON: To safeguard existing trees in the interests of visual amenities.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Prior to commencement of works, full details and specifications of the green roofs shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Green roofs shall be planted with flowering species that provide amenity and biodiversity value at different times of the year. The submission shall include the following:<br style=""></p><ul style=""><li style="margin-left: 15px;">detailed drawings of a roof plan identifying where the green roofs will be located and the measurement of their coverage; this should include other structures on the roof, including the location of PV panels, roof lights, and access points where applicable, and their relationship with the green roof;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">the design of the green roof should be in line with GRO’s code of best practice;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">section drawings demonstrating a minimum substrate depth of no less than 80mm;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">details of the drainage system for the roof;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">details of the planting mix, including a minimum of 16+ species;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">all roofs to be sown with a wide mix of species, the roof should not rely on one species of plant life; and</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">management and maintenance plan, including access arrangements, irrigation, and who is responsible for management and general maintenance actions.</li></ul><div style="">Within a month of the first occupation of the development, evidence must be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority that the green roof(s) have been delivered in line with the approved details unless otherwise agreed in writing. The green roof shall be retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development in accordance with the approved management and maintenance plan.</div><div style=""><br></div><div style="">Reason: To promote biodiversity on site through green roofs.</div>

and&nbsp;</span></p></li><li dir="ltr" style="margin-left: 11pt; list-style-type: disc; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; vertical-align: baseline;"><p dir="ltr" role="presentation" style="line-height: 1.38; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 10pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">All landscaping in accordance with the scheme, when approved, shall be carried out within a period of twelve months from the date on which the development of the site commences or shall be carried out in the first planting (and seeding) season following completion of the development, and shall be maintained to the satisfaction of the local planning authority for a period of ten years, such maintenance to include the replacement of any trees or plants that die, or are severely damaged, seriously diseased, or removed.</span></p></span></div><div style="">REASON: To ensure that the site protects and enhances biodiversity.</div>

<div>No development shall commence, other than works of demolition, until a report (including intrusive investigation/trial pit and monitoring where necessary) demonstrating that the basement development will not increase the potential for groundwater flooding to itself or to the surrounding area during and post-construction has been submitted to the local planning authority for approval. Where groundwater is identified as a potential risk, details of appropriate controls, including flood resilience and/or resistance measures, shall be submitted to the LPA for approval and the approved measures incorporated before the basement is occupied. The basement shall be constructed and completed in accordance with the approved plans in line with BS 8102:2022 Protection of below ground structures against water ingress - code of practice.<br></div><p style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; line-height: 1.38;"><br></p><p style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; line-height: 1.38;">REASON: In the interests of flood risk.</p>

<p>Prior to the commencement of development, a qualified tree specialist must be appointed to provide arboricultural supervision and inspection. The details of this appointment and the specialist's responsibilities must be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The submission should include the methodology and programme for reporting, as well as a timetable for inspections.<br style="">The approved works must be carried out in strict accordance with the approved details. Upon completion of the development and within 2 weeks of the completed works, a report from the appointed arboriculturist must be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority, confirming that all tree protection measures and tree works were carried out in accordance with the approved plans, accompanied by photographs taken at critical stages.<br style=""><br style="">REASON: To ensure that works affecting trees are carried out in a professional and controlled manner, safeguarding their health and long-term viability.&nbsp;</p>

<p data-path-to-node="3" style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">No replacement or new windows or doors shall be installed until full details, including&nbsp;<span style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">1:5 or 1:10 scale elevational drawings</span>&nbsp;and&nbsp;<span style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">1:1 or 1:2 scale sectional drawings,&nbsp;</span>have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall be carried out in strict accordance with the approved details.</p><p data-path-to-node="4" style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">The submitted details must demonstrate the following:</p><ul data-path-to-node="5" style="padding-inline-start: 32px; line-height: 1.15 !important;"><li style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important;"><p data-path-to-node="5,0,0" style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">all new joinery must accurately replicate the design, proportions, and detailing of the existing original windows;</p></li><li style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important;"><p data-path-to-node="5,1,0" style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">units must be&nbsp;<span style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">slimline double glazing</span>&nbsp;with a maximum total thickness of&nbsp;<span style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">12mm,&nbsp;</span>consisting of 4mm glass: 4mm gas : 4mm glass;</p></li><li style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important;"><p data-path-to-node="5,2,0" style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">windows shall feature&nbsp;<span style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">solid (integral) glazing bars</span>&nbsp;and a&nbsp;<span style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">putty-line finish</span>&nbsp;(or a profile that accurately replicates a traditional putty-line); and&nbsp;</p></li><li style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important;"><p data-path-to-node="5,3,0" style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">no visible trickle vents or metallic/perforated spacer bars shall be used.</p></li></ul><p data-path-to-node="7" style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">REASON: To ensure that the appearance of the proposed development is sympathetic to the character and appearance of the c<span style="line-height: 1.15 !important;">onservation area</span>, and to preserve the historic integrity of the host building.&nbsp;</p>
